title: Sampling `tools` / `toolChoice`
description: Request-scoped tool use inside a sampling call, driving a multi-turn tool loop with `tool_use` and `tool_result` content and a `toolUse` stop reason.
question: Does the framework run the sampling tool loop, or only single-shot generation?
why: This was added in the same revision that deprecated sampling, so it is the least likely feature in the protocol to be implemented anywhere. It is catalogued so that absence is recorded rather than assumed.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: no sampling hook, so the client cannot declare `sampling.tools` and the server's SDK refuses to send a tools-bearing request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: no sampling capability is declared (only `roots`), so a sampling request with tools is refused and there is no option to add a handler.
notes.langchain: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: through `session_kwargs` (a `sampling_callback` plus `sampling_capabilities` with `tools`), forwarded unread to the MCP SDK, the two-turn tool loop completed: `tool_use`, the server's `tool_result`, then a final answer. The adapter itself offers neither.
notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: no sampling hook, so the client cannot declare `sampling.tools` and the server's SDK refuses to send a tools-bearing request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: `MCPToolset(sampling_handler=...)` declares plain `sampling` without `tools`, so a tools-bearing request is refused. Declaring `sampling.tools` takes `toolset.client.set_sampling_callback(..., sampling_capabilities=...)` on the wrapped fastmcp `Client`; through that the two-turn tool loop completed.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: no sampling handler and no way to declare `sampling.tools`, so the server's SDK refuses to send the request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench(model_client=...)` answers sampling, but its session declares plain `sampling` without `tools` and `McpSessionActor` never forwards a request's tools to the model client, so a tool-enabled sampling request is refused.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` has no sampling parameter, so it cannot declare `sampling.tools` or answer a tool-enabled sampling request.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): no sampling support, so the server refuses the tool-enabled request ("Client does not support sampling tools capability").
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the client declares no sampling capability, so the server's sampling-with-tools request is refused before any handler could run; the SDK has no sampling hook.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the plugin's `sampling_callback` forwards only messages, system prompt, temperature and max tokens to the kernel's chat service, and the session declares no `sampling.tools` capability, so the server refuses a tool-enabled request.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient(sampling_callback=...)` forwards the callback but not `sampling_capabilities`, so the client never declares `sampling.tools` and the server's tools-enabled `sampling/createMessage` is refused.
notes.pi: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` takes no sampling handler and declares no sampling capability, so the server refuses to send a tool-enabled sampling request.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPSessionManager.createSession` builds `new Client({name: 'MCPClient', version: '1.0.0'})` with no capabilities and no request handlers, and `MCPToolset` takes no client hooks. The tools-enabled `sampling/createMessage` is refused.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` builds its fastmcp `Client` with no sampling handler, so sampling with tools is refused like any other sampling request.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession(read, write)` with no sampling, elicitation, roots or message callback, and neither the server info nor `MCPToolset` takes one, so the server's `sampling/createMessage` with tools got no answer and the tool call failed.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): no sampling hook, so the client cannot declare `sampling.tools` and the server's SDK refuses to send a tools-bearing request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy takes no sampling handler. The server's request is answered only by a `sampling_callback` with `sampling_capabilities` registered on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): there is no sampling handler of any kind, so sampling with tools has no route either.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: `McpSchema.CreateMessageRequest` in MCP Java SDK 2.0.0 has no tools field, so `@McpSampling` cannot declare `sampling.tools` and the server's SDK refuses the tools-bearing request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no sampling handler. Sampling with tools works only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the runtime does not declare sampling tool support, so the server's tool-bearing sampling request failed with "Client does not support sampling tools capability".
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.connect` builds its `ClientSession` from the transport streams alone, with no `sampling_callback`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` take no hook for it, so the client does not declare the capability and the server's request is refused.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpSessionManager` builds the `McpSyncClient` with empty client capabilities and no sampling handler, and neither `McpToolset` nor `McpTool` takes one, so the server refuses the request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `DefaultMcpClient` declares no `sampling` capability, so the server refuses tool-enabled sampling with `Client does not support sampling tools capability`.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: not reachable. The server's SDK refuses the request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`): Kotlin SDK 0.11.1's client capabilities have no sampling `tools` flag, and its `CreateMessageResult` cannot carry a `tool_use` block.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): mcptoolset has no sampling option. A `mcp.ClientOptions.CreateMessageWithToolsHandler` set on the `*mcp.Client` the caller passes as `mcptoolset.Config.Client` answers the server's request, so it works, but only by configuring go-sdk rather than the toolset.

summary: The cell asks whether the adapter runs the sampling tool loop through its own API.
